title: Tiered Outcome Velocity Scorer (TOVS) for inference roadmap
creator: Ivy Chen
description: Proposal and adoption plan for a new prioritization rubric — Tiered Outcome Velocity Scorer (TOVS) — to help the PM team prioritize initiatives for the inference roadmap. TOVS is designed for product decisions where token economics, latency impact, and time-to-outcome interact (e.g., Dedicated autoscaling, runtime batching, console rollouts). It blends outcome tiering with velocity and cost sensitivity multipliers to produce an actionable per-initiative score and a recommended deployment band (Immediate / Next-cycle / Backlog). The doc includes the scoring formula, rubric, worked examples, rollout plan for cross-functional adoption, and success metrics.
motivation: Existing RICE-like artifacts in the organization are numerous and nuanced but often struggle to surface the interaction between latency/throughput economics and time-to-market. TOVS explicitly encodes: outcome tier (strategic/operational/customer-impact), expected delivery velocity, direct token cost delta, latency sensitivity (customer-facing SLA risk), and cohort weight (enterprise vs self-serve). The goal is a reproducible rubric that product, eng, and finance can apply during cycle planning and quarterly roadmap debates.
scoring_formula: TOVS = OutcomeTierScore * VelocityMultiplier * CohortWeight * (1 - CostPenalty) * LatencySensitivityMultiplier. OutcomeTierScore in {5:Strategic, 3:Business, 1:Operational}. VelocityMultiplier = 1 + (max(0, planned_velocity_points - 3) * 0.05) capped at 1.25. CohortWeight in {1.3:Enterprise, 1.0:Hybrid, 0.8:Self-serve}. CostPenalty = normalized token-cost-delta in [0,0.6]. LatencySensitivityMultiplier in {1.25:high, 1.0:medium, 0.85:low}. Final score normalized to 0-100 for presentation.
rubric_guidelines: Outcome tier must be justified with a primary axis: revenue uplift, retention impact, or strategic platform leverage.
Velocity estimate should be a consensus from Eng + PM using planning points; optimistic and pessimistic velocities kept as comments.
Token-cost-delta is the expected per-1M-token cost change relative to baseline and must be normalized by projected monthly token volume for the initiative's target cohort.
Latency sensitivity is decided by customer-facing product owners and requires a target SLO impact statement (e.g., increase average 95th latency by X ms for Y% of requests).
Cohort weight reflects the anticipated percent of traffic and ARR concentration; for early experiments use "self-serve" unless enterprise customers are targeted explicitly.
Use the capped multipliers to avoid single-axis dominance; example: a huge cost penalty will reduce the score but not make it zero — preserves consideration for mission-critical infra work.
Document at least one quantitative metric that will change if the initiative is delivered (e.g., tokens_per_minute, avg_95_latency_ms, $$ per 1M tokens saved, enterprise_retention_pct).
worked_examples: Example 1 - Dedicated Autoscaling policy: OutcomeTierScore=5 (Strategic), VelocityMultiplier=1.10 (estimate 5 points), CohortWeight=1.3 (enterprise pilot), CostPenalty=0.10 (modest token cost increase), LatencySensitivityMultiplier=1.25 (latency-critical). Raw TOVS = 5 * 1.10 * 1.3 * (1 - 0.10) * 1.25 = 8.25. Normalized -> 82 => Recommended band: Immediate (Q2).

Example 2 - Console dashboard: per-route cost breakdown UX: OutcomeTierScore=3 (Business), VelocityMultiplier=1.00, CohortWeight=1.0, CostPenalty=0.00, LatencySensitivityMultiplier=1.0. Raw TOVS=3. Normalized -> 45 => Recommended: Next-cycle (Q3).

Example 3 - Runtime kernel micro-optimization: OutcomeTierScore=1 (Operational), VelocityMultiplier=1.20 (fast engineer work), CohortWeight=0.8 (benefits mostly self-serve), CostPenalty=0.00, LatencySensitivityMultiplier=1.25 (reduces tail latency). Raw TOVS=1 * 1.20 * 0.8 * 1 * 1.25 = 1.2. Normalized -> 28 => Recommended: Backlog / Engineering-chore band (schedule opportunistically).
acceptance_criteria: Cross-functional calibration session completed (PM, Eng, Finance, Research) with at least five representative initiatives scored using TOVS.
Scoring spreadsheet and Confluence template created and accessible to the roadmap working group.
Two retrospective cycles where TOVS output is compared to actual impact (tokens saved, latency change, revenue retention) and calibration adjustments recorded.
Integration of TOVS summary into the quarterly roadmap deck and the cycle planning checklist.
At least one pilot adoption by a product squad (evidence: PRD link and Cycle allocation in the planning doc).
Training workshop delivered to PMs and SWE leads (recording and slide deck linked in artifacts).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overfitting multipliers to historical wins may bias scores. Mitigation: quarterly recalibration and require descriptor fields for why multipliers were chosen.
Risk: Finance pushback on normalized cost penalty assumptions. Mitigation: include finance in the calibration sessions and make normalization rules explicit in the template.
Risk: Velocity estimates gamed to boost score. Mitigation: require engineering sign-off and include optimistic/pessimistic ranges in the scoring sheet.
Risk: Framework perceived as extra overhead. Mitigation: provide a light-mode form (5 fields) and an advanced form (full spreadsheet); light-mode for discovery tickets.
Risk: Latency multipliers interact poorly with bundling of infra and product work. Mitigation: split infra-only initiatives and add a dependency flag; prefer cross-team review for mixed work.
Dependency: needs a small analytics dashboard from Observability to surface token-volume projections per cohort (owner: Analytics infra).
Dependency: update to the roadmap deck template to include TOVS columns (owner: PM Ops).
rollout_plan: Week 0: Socialize TOVS with PM lead group + collect feedback (this ticket).
Week 1: Run calibration workshop with 6 initiatives; update normalization constants based on feedback.
Week 2: Publish Confluence template + scoring Google Sheet; link templates from the planning playbook.
Week 3-4: Pilot scoring in Cycle planning with 2 squads (one infra-heavy, one product-focused).
End of Cycle: Review pilot, collect outcome metrics, and vote on adoption for next quarter.
